messages:
kyle: FYI: saw a sharp saturation spike in us-west-2 GPU pool at ~12:05 UTC. Queue depth climbed fast, small-chat models saw p95 token latency jump. A bunch of requests hit 503s from the global limiter.

maria: darn. any autoscaler activity around then? did warm pool shrink?

sachin: autoscaler triggered a scale-up at 12:06 but warm pool only had 2 prewarmed GPUs. Cold startup on the instance group averaged ~46s which let the admission queue pile up. Model mix that window was skewed to r-glam-13B and several long-seq jobs.

elaine: metrics: gpu_util=97-99% for 3m, queue_peak=~410, p50 input->first-token went 140ms -> 920ms. short billing blip visible on cost dashboard.

kyle: two immediate mitigations I want to try: 1) time-windowed warmup (bump min prewarm during peak hours), 2) change admission from hard reject to soft/weighted shedding so we avoid mass 503s.

maria: soft shedding makes sense. prefer per-customer weight that biases against long seq or high concurrent sessions. soft 429 + Retry-After beats instant 503. also we should extend scale-in cool-down so we don't kill warm nodes too quickly after peaks.

sachin: i've got a prototype rule that uses weighted shedding by active_sessions and seq_len. snippet: 

```
#admission policy
mode: weighted_shed
weight_components:
  - active_sessions
  - avg_sequence_length
triggers:
  queue_threshold: 250
  shed_fraction_at_threshold: 0.4
cooldown_seconds: 120

#behavior: when queue > queue_threshold, reduce per-customer allowed rate by shed_fraction * normalized_weight
```

elaine: nice. canary numbers from staging replay looked promising: with warm_pool_min=6 during noon window + weighted_shed enabled, p95 reduced from ~2.3s -> ~520ms and 503s dropped to <1%.

oncall: ops-bot replayed the incident in staging earlier. placing the config behind a grad-canary flag looks safe. ops-bot will post metrics every 60s during rollout.

kyle: concrete plan: 
1) implement time-windowed warmpool policy in us-west-2: 11:00-15:00 UTC -> min_prewarm=6 (7 day trial)
2) enable weighted_shed behind grad-canary at 10% traffic for 24h starting next peak
3) set scale-in hysteresis to 300s for GPU pools globally

maria: love it. i'll own the canary and SLO dashboards. also request an "admission.shed_rate_by_customer" metric so we can detect over-shedding and rollback quickly.

sachin: i'll open the PR for admission + canary flag. including an opt-out header for enterprise accounts that require strict success guarantees.

elaine: i'll update the runbook and add a quick playbook for cost alerts if warm_pool uplift causes spend > threshold. also add steps to revert canary.

oncall: scheduling canary to start at 13:00 UTC to overlap predicted peak. ops-bot will post a followup summary when metrics stabilize (p95, 503 rate, shed_rate).

kyle: thanks all. want to avoid another midday outage; soft-shedding + warm-window should smooth these spikes. :rocket:
